title: Laxmi Organic Industries Ltd - 543277 - Announcement Under Regulation 30 -SEBI (LODR), 2015

summary.headline: Laxmi Organic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% QoQ with margins up in both businesses; FY26 revenue fell 6% YoY.
summary.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% QoQ across Essentials and Specialties, with sequential margin improvement in both. FY26 revenue declined 6% YoY, driven by feedstock deflation, margin pressure, a one-time Specialties impact and a lost large contract. Management described Middle East-driven spikes in acetic acid and methanol in March-April, with ETAC spreads moderating to about $150-160/t from a peak near $250. Dahej Phase 2 chemical charging is slated for Q1 FY27, with revenue contribution expected in H2 FY27, and Hitachi project output from Q3 FY27. Management declined to give absolute FY27/FY28 revenue numbers, citing market fluidity.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue, Q4 FY26 vs Q3 FY26

financial_highlights.change: -18% YoY per analyst question; management said roughly flat YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Employee cost increase from new sites

segments.name: Essentials
segments.commentary: Revenue grew QoQ in Q4 FY26 with margins improving sequentially; ETAC spreads are the main driver cited, moving from below $100/t in Q3 to about $130/t in Jan-Feb and peaking near $250/t in April before easing to about $150-160/t.

segments.name: Specialties
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 18% YoY in FY26 per analyst, but management said it was roughly flat YoY. Drivers: loss of a structural product (about 10% of top line), deferred shipments moved into Q4, and feedstock deflation. Management said Q4 revenue recovered and margins improved sequentially.

segments.name: Fluorination (Lote)
segments.commentary: Management said it achieved 40-45% of peak revenues in FY26 as planned and has a good order book entering FY27.

segments.name: Ethyl acetate line (Lote)
segments.commentary: World-scale ethyl acetate line started up and dispatches to customers have begun; no capacity or revenue figure given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a good, decent start to FY27 but gave no numeric revenue or margin guidance.
Dahej Phase 2: chemical charging in Q1 FY27, customer sampling thereafter, revenue impact from H2 FY27, ramp-up into FY28 and beyond.
Hitachi project expected to contribute from Q3 FY27, with steady qualification and ramp-up through FY27 under a multiyear contract.
Supply chain digitization project expected to go live in Q2 FY27.

Management declined to give absolute FY27 or FY28 revenue figures (analyst cited INR 3,700-4,000 crore FY27 and about INR 5,000 crore FY28 as ranges to test); said it would give better visibility once conditions settle.
Management said the acetic acid price level around $450-470/t may find a floor, but cautioned it is a point-in-time view.
capex_capacity: Lote fluorination setup achieved 40-45% of peak revenues in FY26, with a good order book entering FY27.
World-scale ethyl acetate line at Lote started up; dispatches have begun.
Dahej Phase 1 is operating and supplying the market; Phase 2 chemical charging is scheduled for Q1 FY27.
Dahej Phase 2 revenue is expected in H2 FY27; analyst cited about INR 1,000 crore spent on Dahej, but management pointed to earlier asset-turn commentary rather than giving a new figure.
Hitachi project expected to start contributing in Q3 FY27.
BRSR report to be released; management cited year-on-year improvements in water and energy intensity at existing sites.
demand_pricing: Acetic acid prices fell to about $300-320/t during FY25 and moved above $400/t in Q3 FY26; they moderated to $350-370/t in Jan-Feb 2026, spiked above $700/t in March-April, and eased to about $450-470/t.
Ethanol (sourced mainly from the Americas) saw firm prices with smaller swings than acetic acid.

Pharma and Printing & Packaging demand was stable in Jan-Feb and spiked in March; Industrial Solutions and Pigments demand was stable to slightly firmer in Q4, with early signs of firmness in Q1 FY27.
Customers responded differently: some built inventory and paid a premium for supply reliability; others bought only what they needed.
Logistics costs have roughly doubled since the Middle East conflict began, with multiple new surcharges; management called this a current negative drag.
Specialties pricing: management said price pass-through is slowed by contracts and customer understanding, with feedstock deflation of about 30% over two years (acetic acid) still feeding through.

qa_highlights.question: What were ETAC spreads in Q4 FY26, what was the peak, and where are they now?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about $130/t in Jan-Feb, rose to about $220/t in March and about $250/t in April, and are now about $150-160/t. Management cited a 12-13 year average of about $220/t excluding COVID highs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $150-160/t range the bottom for the next one to two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to call a bottom, saying it is taking it day-to-day. It said acetic acid around $450-470/t could be a floor while methanol remains high.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Specialties decline beyond the lost contract purely pricing, or also volume and share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: a structural product (about 10% of top line) lost, with an alternative triggered that will mainly contribute in FY27; deferred H1 shipments that came through in Q4; and feedstock deflation. Management said Specialties was roughly flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Will deferrals and pricing issues reverse, and will Specialties grow in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Dahej capacity will contribute from H2 FY27 and ramp up through FY28, but Specialties pricing moves more slowly because of customer contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach INR 3,700-4,000 crore in FY27 and about INR 5,000 crore in FY28, and what is the peak Dahej asset turn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give absolute numbers, citing a fluid environment. On asset turn, it referred to earlier disclosures that split capex between Essentials and Specialties.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: crude, methanol and acetic acid price volatility; ETAC spreads could fall from the current $150-160/t range.
Logistics costs roughly doubled since March 2026, with surcharges still a drag.
Specialties recovery depends on contract-based price pass-through and timing of the alternative product for the lost structural contract (mostly FY27).
Dahej Phase 2 and Hitachi ramp-up timing (Q1, Q2 and Q3 FY27 milestones) and qualification risk.
Interim CFO role; new CFO Amit Jain (ex-Gharda Chemicals) joins 16 June 2026.
Q1 FY27 customer demand update was deferred to the next call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sequential recovery and the operational start-ups, but cautious and non-committal on forward numbers, repeatedly saying the environment is fluid. Management deflected on the ETAC spread floor and on FY27/FY28 revenue targets.
key_quotes: So ending the year strong. I think that's what I would like to call out.
And where we are seeing currently prices for acetic acid is around the levels about $450, $470, where we seemingly think that this will find a floor.
So to put absolute numbers would be immature from my side.
Also thrilled to announce that we have started up our world-scale ethyl acetate setup line at Lote, and we have started already dispatches to customers.

adds.what: Dahej Phase 2 chemical plant (chemical charging Q1 FY27, revenue from H2 FY27)
World-scale ethyl acetate line at Lote (started up, dispatches begun)

growth.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance, only a 'good, decent start' to FY27; Q4 revenue rose 9% QoQ (absolute value not stated), with Dahej Phase 2 (charging Q1 FY27, revenue H2 FY27) and Hitachi (Q3 FY27) timelines backing growth, but FY26 revenue fell 6% YoY.
